edge_explainer: Derailment, slowly - and, importantly, an honestly disclosed one. Revenue: FY26 consensus $776M (-2.6% y/y), near-quarter -4.9%, ttm -4.4%, trailing rev3y +1.3% (three years of going nowhere). The screen's 'forward P/E 8.8x' is a non-GAAP artifact: it is computed on $0.357 non-GAAP FY27 EPS against GAAP trailing EPS of $0.06 and a 2.6% GAAP net margin - a ~6x GAAP-to-non-GAAP gap on a 92%-gross-margin business. On GAAP the multiple is north of 50x; the entire apparent cheapness lives in the adjustment. Mode-B mechanism: GoodRx does not own its economics - discount-card spread sits inside PBM-negotiated networks it neither controls nor durably contracts for, and direct-to-consumer pharma channels disintermediate the cash-pay prescription outright. Three years of flat revenue at 92% gross margin is the signature of an annuity whose volume is being competed away while unit economics look pristine; high gross margin here is asset-lightness, not pricing power. Path: the 2026-02-26 capitulation (-18.8% to $1.99) put in a $1.77 low 153 days ago and the stock is +78.5% off it while still -35.9% y/y, with estimates drifting DOWN over the same window. Per the honesty-alpha doctrine this is the CLEAN case: an impaired business that discloses its impairment plainly, with analysts modelling the decline. Nothing for the detectors to find, therefore no edge to harvest - that is the finding.
top_unverifiable: The PBM-dependency mechanism is a Mode-B derivation, not documented. The 10-K risk factors and PBM/customer-concentration disclosure were not read; the revenue decline is confirmed but the causal attribution is unverified - and the whole structural bear rests on it.
